With C/B = 4.5, the two bands give Dq ≈ 1 817 cm⁻¹ (Δ ≈ 18 200 cm⁻¹) and B ≈ 519 cm⁻¹. I got these by fitting the full d⁶ ligand-field matrix to the two low-spin bands (¹A₁g → ¹T₁g and ¹A₁g → ¹T₂g).

**Setup.** [Co(ox)₃]³⁻ is low-spin d⁶, so the ground term is ¹A₁g. The 16 611 cm⁻¹ band is ¹T₁g and the 23 529 cm⁻¹ band is ¹T₂g.

**Fit.** Two bands fix two unknowns, Dq and B, once C is tied to B. I scanned C by hand until C/B came out at about 4.5, because the fit tool takes C as a fixed number, not as a ratio to B.

| C fixed (cm⁻¹) | Fitted Dq (cm⁻¹) | Fitted B (cm⁻¹) | C/B |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5120 (tool default) | 2012 | 495 | about 10 |
| 2500 | 1826 | 520 | 4.81 |
| 2350 | 1817 | 519 | 4.53 |

The 5120 cm⁻¹ default gives C/B of about 10, so it does not satisfy the stated ratio. The C = 2350 run is the closest to 4.5. It reproduces both bands to within 0.01 cm⁻¹. That is expected, because two parameters are fitted to two bands, so the fit is exactly determined and its quality says nothing about the model.

**Result.** B ≈ 519 cm⁻¹, C ≈ 2 340 cm⁻¹ (C/B ≈ 4.5) and Dq ≈ 1 817 cm⁻¹.
